new_libraries.name: Stimeration
new_libraries.author: RazkarStudio <razkar.studio@proton.me>
new_libraries.sentence: A simple yet powerful timer library that gives you stimulation
new_libraries.paragraph: Provides repeating interval timers and one-shot triggers with millisecond and microsecond resolution, backed by millis() or micros(). Timers and triggers can be paused and resumed without losing track of elapsed time, and a stateless hasElapsed() helper is included for one-off checks that do not need a timer object. Header-only and template-based with no dynamic allocation, suited for AVR-class microcontrollers.

library.name: DTS6012M_UART
library.author: Albert Cornelissen <albert@cornelissen.me>
library.sentence: Enhanced Arduino library for DTS6012M Time-of-Flight sensor with robust error handling, data quality assessment, and calibration.
library.paragraph: Comprehensive v2.0 library for the DTS6012M dToF distance sensor featuring enterprise-grade error handling and recovery, real-time data quality assessment, built-in calibration system, statistics tracking, performance optimization, and comprehensive test framework. Maintains full backward compatibility with v1.x while adding advanced features like circular buffering, configurable parameters, measurement history, and detailed diagnostics. Supports all Arduino architectures with HardwareSerial ports.

library.name: WCB_Client
library.author: Greg Hulette
library.sentence: Client library for joining a Wireless Communication Board (WCB) ESP-NOW network.
library.paragraph: Allows any ESP32-based device to participate as a native peer in a WCB network. Supports unicast and broadcast text commands with automatic fragmentation for long commands (e.g. saving large stored sequences), raw binary forwarding for Pololu/Maestro servo packets via WCBStream, ETM heartbeat and ACK tracking, board online/offline status callbacks, and communication with an out-of-band special peer such as NaviCore via enableSpecialPeer(). A raw-packet hook (onRawPacket/sendRawPacket) lets custom protocols — such as firmware OTA — ride the same ESP-NOW mesh. setIdentity() advertises the device over WDP so WCBs discover it by name and firmware version automatically (the mesh twin of the serial WDP-DA device-announce model), and onNeighbor()/getNeighbor() consume the same WDP adverts to learn every WCB and client on the mesh — alias, firmware, capabilities, controller link and Maestro IDs. With auto-join (on by default) the device also registers regular WCBs it hears as ESP-NOW peers live and remembers them across reboots, so it discovers the fleet once and never needs wcb_quantity to cover it.
